findings.verification: Static review only; proposal is not implemented or executed.

findings.acceptance_criteria: Downloaded archive entry names remain distinct and usable on supported platforms without losing content.
findings.existing_coverage_credit: Filename sanitization and collision logic already have substantial tests; PATCH-09 adds archive body integrity.
implementation_notes: Locate the actual filename-byte budget and test Windows reserved basenames with/without extensions.
Combine multi-byte truncation with case/NFC collisions and suffix assignment.
Extract generated archives on supported OS fixtures if portable extraction is part of the contract.
findings.observed_gap: Path punctuation/Unicode collision tests do not necessarily cover CON/PRN/AUX, trailing dots/spaces and truncation near the filename byte limit.
findings.risk_or_open_decision: This is a portability gap hypothesis; verify upstream tests and exact limit before changing naming conventions.
findings.title: Export filename portability needs Windows reserved-name boundary cases
findings.verification: Static review only; proposal is not implemented or executed.

findings.acceptance_criteria: The cache budget is accurately named/documented and measured behavior matches that contract.
findings.existing_coverage_credit: Cache eviction/byte admission and PATCH-06 edge tests exist.
implementation_notes: Document whether maxBytes means source bytes or estimated retained object bytes.
Add expansion-heavy loader fixtures and eviction/admission assertions.
Measure process memory separately if a true memory budget is required; introduce a weight callback only with a clear contract.
findings.observed_gap: File size is a useful admission estimate but parsed objects can expand or retain extra data; naming can imply a stronger memory guarantee than implemented.
findings.risk_or_open_decision: Do not treat object-size expansion alone as a bug if the documented budget is source bytes.
findings.title: Cache maxBytes is not demonstrated as a retained-memory bound
findings.verification: Static review only; proposal is not implemented or executed.

findings.acceptance_criteria: No unreviewed path follows a symlink outside the allowed static root under the adopted policy.
findings.existing_coverage_credit: Production server tests already cover ordinary assets and path handling.
implementation_notes: Inspect actual static-file dispatch and document the trusted-build assumption.
Serve a fixture dist tree containing an internal symlink to an outside sentinel.
Assert the chosen rejection/containment contract and preserve legitimate asset behavior.
findings.observed_gap: Lexical path.resolve containment alone cannot prove containment after a symlink; the practical risk depends on whether build output is trusted and writable.
findings.risk_or_open_decision: This is a medium-confidence hardening opportunity, not a demonstrated production data leak.
findings.title: Static asset realpath containment is not exercised against symlinked build files
findings.verification: Static review only; proposal is not implemented or executed.

findings.acceptance_criteria: Documented cancellation stops work where supported and cannot return a misleading successful or null result.
findings.existing_coverage_credit: Ordinary network failure/status handling is tested.
implementation_notes: Decide whether caller-provided AbortSignal belongs on client defaults, operation options or both.
Add delayed-response/stream tests with abort before connect and during body transfer.
Verify typed abort errors and cleanup without converting cancellation into not-found.
findings.observed_gap: Long local/HTTP exports can outlive a caller’s intent; the current API does not expose an obvious unified cancellation/timeout option.
findings.risk_or_open_decision: This is a design-dependent improvement, not a reproduced API bug.
findings.title: SDK timeout and cancellation behavior has no explicit public contract

scope: Static review of the supplied archive plus implemented targeted regressions and limited supplemental execution. Not an assertion that every possible gap was found.

complexity.1: One narrow test or guard, no new environment.
complexity.2: Small focused suite or helper change.
complexity.3: Multiple modules or joined fixture/transport integration.
complexity.4: Browser/process/platform matrix or substantial harness work.

scoring.confidence: 0-100 confidence that the stated gap/opportunity exists in this archive, not probability that an unexecuted patch passes. 100 may reflect directly observed absence of an E2E harness or a deterministic reproduction; lower values indicate policy/input uncertainty.

priority.P0: False-green verification or equivalent release-blocking assurance failure.
priority.P1: Data integrity, destructive-operation safety, primary workflows, security boundaries, or broad assurance holes.
priority.P2: Important edge cases, portability, maintainability, observability or design-dependent hardening.
priority.P3: Optional polish (no entries assigned in this audit).

scoring.sort: Priority first, then higher confidence, then lower complexity, then stable finding ID. IDs remain stable and are not the rank.

status.implemented: Code/test patch exists; canonical execution remains unverified unless explicitly stated.
status.partial: Browser code exists, but dependency/lock setup and first browser execution remain outstanding.
status.pending: Reviewed improvement with detailed implementation specification, not implemented.
